question: Which five-year plan was based on the ideas of Mahalanobis?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Second five-year plan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Second Five-Year Plan (1956–61) was based on the Mahalanobis Model, formulated by statistician-economist Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis. (द्वितीय पंचवर्षीय योजना — महालनोबिस मॉडल)

 

• The plan's central strategy was rapid industrialisation with emphasis on heavy and basic industries (capital goods sector), on the logic that a strong industrial base would sustain long-term growth.

 

• It is often called the "Industry Plan" and led to the setting up of major public-sector steel plants such as Bhilai, Rourkela and Durgapur.

 

• Mahalanobis is also renowned as the founder of the Indian Statistical Institute (ISI), Kolkata, and a pioneer of large-scale sample surveys in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The First Five-Year Plan (1951–56) was based on the Harrod-Domar model and focused on agriculture.

 

• The Third Five-Year Plan (1961–66) aimed for a "self-reliant and self-generating" economy but was disrupted by the 1962 and 1965 wars and the 1965-66 drought.

 

NOTE

 

• Fourth five-year plan (Option 1): Focused on the twin objectives of "growth with stability" and "progressive achievement of self-reliance"; the Gadgil formula for resource allocation to states was introduced during this period.

 

• Third five-year plan (Option 2): Based on the idea of a self-reliant economy, but not on the Mahalanobis model itself.

 

• First five-year plan (Option 3): Based on the Harrod-Domar growth model, prioritising agriculture and irrigation.

question: Little Andaman in the south is separated from the Nicobar Islands by the ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 10 Degree Channel.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 10° Channel separates the Andaman Islands (specifically Little Andaman, its southernmost island) from the Nicobar Islands, and lies roughly along the 10° North latitude. (10 डिग्री चैनल — अंडमान व निकोबार द्वीप समूह के बीच)

 

• Both island groups together form the Union Territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands in the Bay of Bengal.

 

• The channel is an important international shipping route, connecting the Indian Ocean/Bay of Bengal traffic passing between Southeast Asia and the Indian subcontinent.

 

• Further south, the Great Channel separates the Nicobar Islands (Great Nicobar) from Sumatra, Indonesia.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Duncan Passage separates South Andaman from Little Andaman.

 

• The Ten Degree Channel is about 150 km wide and is one of the key navigational channels of the Indian Ocean.

 

NOTE

 

• 8 Degree Channel (Option 1): Separates the Lakshadweep/Minicoy island from the Maldives, not related to Andaman-Nicobar.

 

• 7 Degree Channel (Option 3): No standard named channel by this exact name in this region; it is not associated with Little Andaman–Nicobar separation.

 

• 9 Degree Channel (Option 4): Separates Lakshadweep islands (Amini, Kadmat, etc.) from Minicoy Island, unrelated to the Andaman-Nicobar group.

question: For which of the following films, has Akshay Kumar won a National award?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rustom.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Akshay Kumar won the National Film Award for Best Actor at the 64th National Film Awards for his performance in the 2016 film Rustom. (रुस्तम फिल्म — अक्षय कुमार को राष्ट्रीय फिल्म पुरस्कार)

 

• Rustom is loosely based on the real-life K.M. Nanavati vs State of Maharashtra case (1959), a famous naval officer murder trial.

 

• This remains, as of the exam's currency, Akshay Kumar's only National Film Award (Best Actor) win in his career.

 

• The National Film Awards are presented annually by the Directorate of Film Festivals, Government of India, and are among the most prestigious film honours in the country.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Akshay Kumar has also received multiple Filmfare Awards, including Filmfare Best Actor for Rustom (2017).

 

• He was awarded the Padma Shri in 2009 for his contribution to the arts.

 

NOTE

 

• Raksha Bandhan (Option 1): A 2022 family drama film starring Akshay Kumar; it did not win him a National Award.

 

• Mission Mangal (Option 2): A 2019 film based on India's Mars Orbiter Mission in which Akshay Kumar starred; it did not fetch him a National Award.

 

• Bell Bottom (Option 4): A 2021 spy-thriller starring Akshay Kumar based on real-life hijacking incidents; no National Award was won for this film.

question: Which Indian javelin thrower has been suspended in 2022 (till 2025) for doping?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shivpal Singh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Shivpal Singh, an Indian javelin thrower who represented India at the 2020 Tokyo Olympics, was suspended by the National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA) for a doping violation, with the ban running till 2025.

 

• He had earlier won gold at the 2019 South Asian Games and set his personal-best/national-level marks in javelin throw before the ban.

 

• Doping suspensions in India are adjudicated by NADA under the rules of the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) framework.

 

• This is distinct from fellow javelin thrower Neeraj Chopra, who has no doping-related suspension and remains India's premier javelin star.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• NADA India was set up in 2005 to promote and coordinate dope-free sport in the country.

 

• Athletes found guilty of doping violations can face bans ranging from a few months to several years (and life bans for repeat offenders) under WADA's Anti-Doping Code.

 

NOTE

 

• Neeraj Chopra (Option 2): India's Olympic gold-medallist javelin thrower (Tokyo 2020); not suspended for doping.

 

• Kashinath Naik (Option 3): An Indian javelin thrower and Commonwealth Games medallist, not associated with this 2022 doping suspension.

 

• Devendra Jhajharia (Option 4): A celebrated Indian Paralympic javelin thrower and two-time Paralympic gold medallist, unrelated to this doping case.

question: Lingaraja Temple is situated in which of the following states of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odisha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Lingaraja Temple is located in Bhubaneswar, Odisha, and is dedicated to Lord Harihara (a combined form of Shiva and Vishnu), locally worshipped as Tribhubaneswar. (लिंगराज मंदिर, भुवनेश्वर — ओडिशा)

 

• It was built primarily during the reign of the Somavamshi (Keshari) dynasty, around the 11th century CE, with later additions by the Ganga rulers.

 

• It is constructed in the classic Kalinga style of architecture, characterised by a curvilinear deul (tower), and stands about 55 metres (180 feet) tall.

 

• The temple is one of the largest temples in Bhubaneswar, which is often called the "Temple City of India".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The temple complex houses over 150 subsidiary shrines within its compound.

 

• Bhubaneswar also hosts other famous temples like the Mukteshvara and Rajarani temples, part of the same Kalinga temple tradition.

 

NOTE

 

• Karnataka (Option 2): Known for temples such as those at Belur, Halebidu and Pattadakal (Hoysala and Chalukya architecture), not the Lingaraja Temple.

 

• Maharashtra (Option 3): Known for cave temples like Ajanta-Ellora, not the Lingaraja Temple.

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 4): Known for Dravidian-style temples like the Brihadeeswarar Temple, Thanjavur; the Lingaraja Temple is not located there.

question:
Which of the following statements is/are NOT correct?
I. Force per unit volume is called pressure.
II. Liquids can exert pressure on walls of containers.
III. Force acting on an object can cause a change in it state of motion but not its shape.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only I and III.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement I is incorrect: Pressure is defined as force per unit area (Pressure = Force/Area), not force per unit volume. Force per unit volume is a different quantity (sometimes called force density), not pressure.

 

• Statement II is correct: Liquids at rest do exert pressure on the walls and base of their containers, and this pressure acts perpendicular to the surface at every point (this is the basis of hydrostatic pressure).

 

• Statement III is incorrect: A force acting on an object can change both its state of motion (speed/direction) and its shape — e.g., squeezing a rubber ball deforms it (changes shape) while also possibly moving it. It is wrong to say force cannot change shape.

 

• Since Statements I and III are the incorrect ones, and Statement II is correct, the statements that are "NOT correct" are I and III.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The SI unit of pressure is the pascal (Pa), equal to 1 newton per square metre (N/m²).

 

• Newton's laws describe how force affects motion, while the concept of elasticity/deformation (stress-strain) describes how force affects shape — both effects can occur simultaneously.

 

NOTE

 

• Only I and II (Option 1): Incorrect, because Statement II ("liquids can exert pressure on walls of containers") is actually a correct/true statement, not an incorrect one.

 

• Only III (Option 2): Incomplete — Statement I is also incorrect (pressure is force per unit area, not volume), so III alone is not the full answer.

 

• I, II and III (Option 3): Incorrect, because Statement II is a true statement and should not be included among the "not correct" statements.

question: The Mahanadi basin does not extend over which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnataka.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Mahanadi river originates near Sihawa in the Chhattisgarh highlands and flows through Chhattisgarh and Odisha before draining into the Bay of Bengal. (महानदी नदी बेसिन)

 

• Its drainage basin also extends into parts of Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, and Maharashtra, but does not touch Karnataka, which lies far to the south and drains mainly into peninsular rivers like the Krishna and Cauvery systems.

 

• The Mahanadi basin is one of the major river basins of Peninsular/East-Central India and is significant for irrigation and hydel projects such as the Hirakud Dam in Odisha, one of the world's longest earthen dams.

 

• Major tributaries of the Mahanadi include the Seonath, Hasdeo, Mand, Ib, Ong and Tel.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Hirakud Dam on the Mahanadi in Odisha was one of independent India's first major multipurpose river valley projects, commissioned in 1957.

 

• The Mahanadi's total length is about 890 km, and its basin area is roughly 1.4 lakh sq. km.

 

NOTE

 

• Chhattisgarh (Option 2): The Mahanadi originates here and a large part of its upper basin lies in this state.

 

• Jharkhand (Option 3): A smaller portion of the Mahanadi basin extends into southern Jharkhand.

 

• Odisha (Option 4): The lower Mahanadi basin and its delta lie substantially in Odisha, before the river meets the Bay of Bengal.

question: herSTART, an initiative implemented by the Gujarat University Startup and Entrepreneurship, was launched by ______ in October 2022.
solution_text:
The correct answer is President Draupadi Murmu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• herSTART is a start-up platform for women entrepreneurs, launched under the Gujarat University Startup and Entrepreneurship Council (GUSEC).

 

• It was launched by President Droupadi Murmu in October 2022, during her visit to Gujarat, where she also inaugurated/laid foundation stones for other education and tribal-development projects of the Gujarat government.

 

• The initiative aims to support, mentor and fund women-led start-ups, encouraging greater participation of women in India's entrepreneurial ecosystem.

 

• Draupadi Murmu took office as the 15th President of India in July 2022, becoming the first tribal woman to hold the post.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• GUSEC (Gujarat University Startup and Entrepreneurship Council) is a Section-8 (not-for-profit) company that runs incubation and acceleration programmes for start-ups in Gujarat.

 

• The launch of herSTART is part of the broader push under the Startup India initiative to promote women-led entrepreneurship.

 

NOTE

 

• Prime Minister Narendra Modi (Option 1): Did not launch herSTART; he heads the Government of India and frequently promotes Startup India initiatives generally, but this specific launch was by the President.

 

• Defence Minister Rajnath Singh (Option 3): Not connected to the launch of herSTART.

 

• Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman (Option 4): Not connected to the launch of herSTART; she oversees financial and economic policy matters, not this specific launch.

question: Who was the first Indian Army officer to be promoted to the rank of field marshal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sam Manekshaw.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Field Marshal Sam Hormusji Framji Jamshedji Manekshaw was promoted to the rank of Field Marshal in January 1973, becoming the first Indian Army officer to hold this five-star rank.

 

• He is best remembered for masterminding India's decisive victory in the 1971 Indo-Pakistan War, which led to the creation of Bangladesh.

 

• Field Marshal is the highest rank in the Indian Army — a rare, largely ceremonial five-star rank conferred only in recognition of exceptional distinguished service; it does not have a fixed retirement age.

 

• K.M. Cariappa became the second Indian to be conferred the rank of Field Marshal, in 1986 — well after Manekshaw. (सैम मानेकशॉ — भारत के प्रथम फील्ड मार्शल)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India has had only two Field Marshals to date: Sam Manekshaw (1973) and K.M. Cariappa (1986).

 

• Manekshaw also served as India's 8th Chief of the Army Staff and was awarded the Padma Vibhushan and Padma Bhushan.

 

NOTE

 

• Vikram Batra (Option 1): A Param Vir Chakra awardee, martyred during the 1999 Kargil War; he was a Captain, not a Field Marshal.

 

• Karam Singh (Option 2): The first recipient of the Param Vir Chakra (India's highest wartime gallantry award), for the 1947-48 Indo-Pak war; not a Field Marshal.

 

• K.M. Cariappa (Option 4): India's first Indian Commander-in-Chief of the Army post-independence, and later India's second Field Marshal (1986) — after Manekshaw, not before.

question: The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 of the Indian constitution has added which of the following in the preamble to the constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Secular.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, often called the "Mini-Constitution", added the words "Socialist", "Secular", and "Integrity" (changing "Unity of the Nation" to "Unity and Integrity of the Nation") to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution. (42वां संविधान संशोधन — पंथनिरपेक्ष शब्द जोड़ा गया)

 

• This amendment was passed during the Emergency (1975-77) under Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, based on recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.

 

• The original 1950 Preamble already described India as a "Sovereign Democratic Republic" — these three words were present from the outset and were not added in 1976.

 

• The 42nd Amendment is the only amendment so far to have altered the wording of the Preamble.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• After the 1976 amendment, the Preamble describes India as a "Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic".

 

• The 42nd Amendment also made several other changes, such as adding Fundamental Duties (Article 51A) to the Constitution.

 

NOTE

 

• Sovereign (Option 2): Was part of the original 1950 Preamble, not added by the 42nd Amendment.

 

• Democratic (Option 3): Also part of the original 1950 Preamble.

 

• Republic (Option 4): Also part of the original 1950 Preamble, describing India's form of government from the very beginning.

question: How many gold medals did India win in 2020 Tokyo Olympic Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India won 1 gold medal at the Tokyo 2020 Olympic Games (held in 2021 due to COVID-19), won by Neeraj Chopra in the Men's Javelin Throw. (टोक्यो ओलंपिक 2020 — नीरज चोपड़ा, भाला फेंक स्वर्ण पदक)

 

• This was independent India's first-ever Olympic gold medal in athletics, and only the second individual gold medal in Olympic history for India after Abhinav Bindra (shooting, 2008 Beijing).

 

• India's overall medal tally at Tokyo 2020 was 7 medals: 1 gold, 2 silver, and 4 bronze — its best-ever Olympic performance at the time.

 

• Silver medals came from Mirabai Chanu (weightlifting) and Ravi Kumar Dahiya (wrestling); bronze medals came from PV Sindhu (badminton), Lovlina Borgohain (boxing), the Men's Hockey Team, and Bajrang Punia (wrestling).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's previous best Olympic showing was 6 medals at the 2012 London Olympics.

 

• Neeraj Chopra's winning throw was 87.58 metres.

 

NOTE

 

• 2 (Option 1): Incorrect — India won only one gold medal, not two.

 

• 0 (Option 3): Incorrect — India did secure one gold medal (Neeraj Chopra), so the count is not zero.

 

• 3 (Option 4): Incorrect — overstates the gold medal count; India's tally included golds, silvers, and bronzes totalling 7 medals, but only 1 was gold.

question: Which among the following states ranked 1st amongst "Achievers" states in the Logistics Ease Across Different States (LEADS) Report 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Logistics Ease Across Different States (LEADS) 2022 Report, released by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, ranks Indian states/UTs on logistics performance into categories: Achievers, Fast Movers, and Aspirers.

 

• Among states in the "Achievers" category (the highest-performing tier), Maharashtra ranked 1st in the LEADS 2022 report.

 

• The LEADS index assesses states on parameters like infrastructure, services, operating/regulatory environment, and timeliness of cargo movement, aiming to improve logistics efficiency across India.

 

• The report is part of the government's broader push under the National Logistics Policy to bring down India's logistics costs.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other states featured in the "Achievers" category of LEADS 2022 included Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Haryana, Karnataka, Odisha, Punjab, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, and Uttar Pradesh, among others.

 

• Gujarat has historically topped the overall LEADS rankings in several editions of the survey.

 

NOTE

 

• Assam (Option 2): Featured among the "Achievers" states but did not rank 1st in LEADS 2022.

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 3): Also featured among "Achievers" states but was not ranked 1st.

 

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 4): Also featured among "Achievers" states but was not ranked 1st.

question: Which country will host the ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2023 (13th edition, ODI format) was hosted by India, held from 5 October to 19 November 2023. (आईसीसी क्रिकेट विश्व कप 2023 — भारत की मेजबानी)

 

• This was the fourth time India hosted the tournament (either solely or jointly), after 1987, 1996, and 2011.

 

• The final was played at the Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad, where Australia defeated India to win their 6th World Cup title.

 

• Virat Kohli was the tournament's highest run-scorer, and Mohammed Shami was the highest wicket-taker.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's team reached the final unbeaten through the league stage and semi-final but lost to Australia in the final.

 

• The 2023 World Cup used a single round-robin format with 10 teams.

 

NOTE

 

• Australia (Option 1): Won the 2023 World Cup as a team but did not host it.

 

• South Africa (Option 2): Hosted the 2003 Cricket World Cup (jointly with Zimbabwe and Kenya), not the 2023 edition.

 

• West Indies (Option 4): Hosted the 2007 Cricket World Cup, not the 2023 edition; the West Indies team also failed to qualify for the 2023 tournament.

question: The preamble of the Indian constitution is borrowed from the constitution of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is United States of America.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The concept and opening phrase of the Indian Constitution's Preamble — "We, the people of India..." — is borrowed from the Preamble of the United States Constitution, which begins "We the People of the United States...". (संविधान की प्रस्तावना — अमेरिका के संविधान से प्रेरित)

 

• The Preamble is regarded as the "identity card" or "soul" of the Constitution, summarising its guiding philosophy and objectives — Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic, Justice, Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity.

 

• It was adopted on 26 November 1949 along with the rest of the Constitution and came into effect on 26 January 1950.

 

• In the landmark Kesavananda Bharati case (1973), the Supreme Court held that the Preamble is part of the Constitution and can be amended, but not in a manner that alters its "basic structure".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Preamble was amended once, by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, which added "Socialist", "Secular" and "Integrity".

 

• India's Constitution borrowed features from many countries — e.g., Fundamental Rights from the USA, Directive Principles from Ireland, and the parliamentary system from Britain.

 

NOTE

 

• USSR / present Russia (Option 1): India's Fundamental Duties (Article 51A) were inspired by the erstwhile USSR's constitution, not the Preamble.

 

• Canada (Option 2): India borrowed the concept of a strong Centre in a federal setup (quasi-federal structure) from Canada, not the Preamble.

 

• Britain (Option 3): India borrowed features like parliamentary government, rule of law, and single citizenship from Britain, not the wording of the Preamble.

question: ______ was the leading producing State of manganese ore accounting for 33% of total production during 2019-20 in India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Indian Bureau of Mines / Indian Minerals Yearbook data, Madhya Pradesh was the leading manganese ore producing state in India during 2019-20, accounting for around 33% of total national production. (मध्य प्रदेश — भारत में मैंगनीज अयस्क का सबसे बड़ा उत्पादक राज्य)

 

• Maharashtra ranked second (around 25%), followed by Odisha (around 18%), with Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh contributing smaller shares (around 11% each).

 

• Key manganese-mining belts in Madhya Pradesh lie in the Balaghat and Chhindwara districts.

 

• Manganese is a vital ferroalloy metal, primarily used in steel-making (as a deoxidiser and alloying agent) and in the manufacture of dry-cell batteries.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India ranks among the top manganese ore producing countries globally, though it also imports high-grade manganese ore for specific industrial uses.

 

• The Central Provinces manganese belt (spanning Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra) has historically been India's most important manganese-producing tract.

 

NOTE

 

• Odisha (Option 1): An important manganese producer (notably in Bonai, Kalahandi, Koraput belts) but ranked third, not first, in 2019-20.

 

• Maharashtra (Option 3): The second-largest producer in 2019-20 (Nagpur-Bhandara belt), behind Madhya Pradesh.

 

• Karnataka (Option 4): A smaller manganese producer compared to Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Odisha.

question: A ______ account is one which is maintained by an Indian Bank in the foreign countries usually in the currency of that country for the purpose of carrying out transactions there.
solution_text:
The correct answer is NOSTRO.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A NOSTRO account is an account that an Indian bank maintains in a foreign country, denominated in the currency of that foreign country, used to settle foreign exchange and international trade transactions. (नॉस्ट्रो खाता — विदेश में भारतीय बैंक का खाता)

 

• "Nostro" is Latin for "ours" — i.e., "our account, held by them (the foreign bank)".

 

• In contrast, a VOSTRO account is the account of a foreign bank held with an Indian (domestic) bank, usually in Indian Rupees — "Vostro" means "yours" in Latin.

 

• Together, Nostro and Vostro accounts facilitate smooth cross-border banking and foreign exchange settlement between correspondent banks.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• A related term, "Loro account", refers to an account of a third bank held with another bank, used when referring to it from a third party's perspective.

 

• These account types are central to correspondent banking relationships that enable international remittances and trade finance.

 

NOTE

 

• VOSTRO (Option 2): The account of a foreign bank held with a domestic (Indian) bank — the reverse of a Nostro account.

 

• LIBOR (Option 3): The London Interbank Offered Rate, a benchmark interest rate at which banks lent to one another in the London market (now largely phased out and replaced by SOFR); it is an interest rate, not an account type.

 

• MIBOR (Option 4): The Mumbai Interbank Offer Rate, India's domestic benchmark interest rate for interbank lending, also not an account type.

question: Which of the following disease is not caused by a mosquito bite?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hepatitis.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Hepatitis is inflammation of the liver, most commonly caused by viral infection (Hepatitis A, B, C, D, E), spread through contaminated food/water (A, E) or blood and body fluids (B, C, D) — it is not transmitted by mosquito bite. (हेपेटाइटिस — मच्छर जनित रोग नहीं है)

 

• Dengue is caused by the dengue virus, transmitted by the female Aedes aegypti mosquito.

 

• Malaria is caused by the Plasmodium parasite, transmitted by the bite of the female Anopheles mosquito.

 

• Elephantiasis (Lymphatic Filariasis) is caused by thread-like parasitic worms (Wuchereria bancrofti, etc.), transmitted by the bite of Culex mosquitoes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other mosquito-borne diseases include Chikungunya, Zika virus, Japanese Encephalitis, and Yellow Fever.

 

• Hepatitis B and C can also spread through unsafe injections, unscreened blood transfusions, and from mother to child during childbirth.

 

NOTE

 

• Elephantiasis (Option 1): Caused by filarial parasites transmitted through Culex mosquito bites, hence mosquito-borne.

 

• Dengue (Option 2): Caused by dengue virus transmitted via Aedes aegypti mosquito bites, hence mosquito-borne.

 

• Malaria (Option 3): Caused by Plasmodium parasites transmitted via Anopheles mosquito bites, hence mosquito-borne.

question: Who among the following devised a policy that came to be known as the Doctrine of Lapse?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Dalhousie.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Doctrine of Lapse was devised and vigorously implemented by Lord Dalhousie, Governor-General of India from 1848 to 1856. (व्यपगत का सिद्धांत — लॉर्ड डलहौजी)

 

• Under this policy, if an Indian ruler died without a natural male heir, his adopted heir would not be recognised, and the princely state would "lapse" (be annexed) into British territory — unless the adoption had prior British sanction.

 

• States annexed under this doctrine included Satara (1848), Jaitpur and Sambalpur (1849), Udaipur (1852), Jhansi (1853), and Nagpur (1854).

 

• The doctrine caused widespread resentment among Indian princely rulers and is considered one of the significant causes of the Revolt of 1857, notably fuelling the anger of the Rani of Jhansi.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lord Dalhousie also annexed Awadh (Oudh) in 1856 on grounds of misgovernance, using a separate justification (not the Doctrine of Lapse itself).

 

• He is also credited with introducing India's first railway line and telegraph system.

 

NOTE

 

• Lord Hastings (Option 2): Governor-General known for the Third Anglo-Maratha War and expanding British paramountcy through the Subsidiary Alliance system, not the Doctrine of Lapse.

 

• Lord Cornwallis (Option 3): Known for introducing the Permanent Settlement (1793) in Bengal and civil service reforms, not the Doctrine of Lapse.

 

• Lord Minto (Option 4): Known for the Minto-Morley Reforms (1909), which introduced separate electorates; not associated with the Doctrine of Lapse.

question: Which of the following is NOT an output device?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bar code reader.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A Bar code reader (scanner) is an input device that optically scans barcodes and converts them into digital data for the computer to process — it does not produce output. (बार कोड रीडर — इनपुट डिवाइस)

 

• A Plotter is an output device used to print high-quality vector graphics such as engineering drawings, architectural plans, and large-format charts.

 

• A Monitor (VDU) is an output device that visually displays text, images, and video processed by the computer.

 

• A Dot matrix printer is an output device that prints characters/images using a matrix of pins striking an ink ribbon, commonly used for multi-part forms and receipts.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other common input devices include the keyboard, mouse, scanner, joystick, and microphone.

 

• Other common output devices include speakers, projectors, and headphones.

 

NOTE

 

• Plotter (Option 1): An output device for producing large, precise line-drawings/graphics.

 

• Monitor (Option 2): An output device that displays visual output from the computer.

 

• Dot matrix printer (Option 3): An output device that prints text/graphics using an impact printing mechanism.

question: In which of the following ways of heat transfer no medium is required?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Radiation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Radiation is the mode of heat transfer that occurs through electromagnetic waves and does not require any medium — it can even travel through a vacuum. (विकिरण — बिना माध्यम के ऊष्मा स्थानांतरण)

 

• This is exactly how heat from the Sun reaches the Earth, travelling across the vacuum of space.

 

• Conduction is heat transfer through direct molecular contact within a solid (or between touching bodies) — it requires a material medium.

 

• Convection is heat transfer through the actual bulk movement of fluid particles (liquids/gases) — it too requires a material medium (a fluid).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• All bodies above absolute zero temperature emit thermal radiation; the amount and wavelength depend on the body's temperature (Stefan-Boltzmann Law, Wien's Displacement Law).

 

• A vacuum flask (thermos) minimises heat loss by reducing conduction, convection, and radiation simultaneously through its double-walled, evacuated, silvered design.

 

NOTE

 

• Radiation and Conduction both (Option 1): Incorrect, since conduction does require a medium (it cannot occur through vacuum).

 

• Conduction (Option 2): Requires physical/molecular contact — needs a medium; incorrect for this question.

 

• Convection (Option 3): Requires movement of a fluid medium (liquid or gas); cannot occur without one, so incorrect for this question.

question: In which year was the Arms Act disallowing Indians from possessing arms passed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1878.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian Arms Act, 1878 was enacted by the British colonial government, requiring Indians to obtain a licence to possess, manufacture, or sell firearms — a restriction that largely did not apply to Europeans. (शस्त्र अधिनियम, 1878)

 

• It was passed under Viceroy Lord Lytton, in the aftermath of the Revolt of 1857, as part of a broader set of repressive measures to curb the threat of armed Indian resistance.

 

• The same year (1878) also saw the passage of the highly controversial Vernacular Press Act, which curtailed the freedom of Indian-language newspapers — both laws are often studied together as tools of colonial control under Lytton.

 

• The Arms Act was seen as racially discriminatory, since it institutionalised the disarming of the general Indian population while exempting the European community.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Vernacular Press Act, 1878 was repealed in 1882 under Lord Ripon, partly in response to strong Indian public protest.

 

• The Arms Act framework, in modified form, continued to influence subsequent arms-control legislation in India, including the post-independence Arms Act, 1959.

 

NOTE

 

• 1876 (Option 1): Not the year of the Arms Act; 1876 saw events like the Royal Titles Act declaring Queen Victoria "Empress of India".

 

• 1877 (Option 3): Not the year of the Arms Act; 1877 was the year of the Delhi Durbar proclaiming Victoria as Empress of India.

 

• 1875 (Option 4): Not the year of the Arms Act; no major restrictive legislation of this type was passed in 1875.

question: In the higher latitudes (50° – 70°) of Northern hemisphere the spectacular Coniferous forests are found. These are also called as ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Taiga.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Coniferous forest belt found in the higher latitudes (50°-70°N) of the Northern Hemisphere, spanning across countries like Russia, Canada, and Scandinavia, is known as the Taiga (also called the Boreal Forest). (टैगा वन — शंकुधारी वन पट्टी)

 

• Taiga forests are dominated by evergreen coniferous trees such as pine, fir, and spruce, adapted to long, cold winters and short summers.

 

• They form the largest terrestrial biome on Earth by area, stretching in a continuous belt across North America and Eurasia.

 

• The Tundra biome lies further north (poleward of the Taiga, roughly beyond 60°-70°N up to the poles), characterised by permafrost and the absence of trees.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Taiga soils are typically acidic and podzolic, low in nutrients due to slow decomposition in the cold climate.

 

• Wildlife commonly found in the Taiga includes moose, wolves, bears, and lynx.

 

NOTE

 

• Veld (Option 1): Open grassland/savanna regions of South Africa, unrelated to coniferous forests.

 

• Tundra (Option 2): The treeless, permanently frozen biome found beyond the Taiga (poleward), not the coniferous forest belt itself.

 

• Llanos (Option 3): Tropical grassland plains found in Venezuela and Colombia (South America), unrelated to coniferous forests.

question: Which of the following shortcut key is used to save a file in MS-Word 365?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ctrl + S.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ctrl + S is the standard keyboard shortcut used to save the currently open file in MS-Word 365, as well as in virtually all other Microsoft Office applications and most Windows software. (Ctrl + S — फ़ाइल सेव करने का शॉर्टकट)

 

• If the file has not been saved before, pressing Ctrl + S opens the "Save As" dialog box to let the user choose a file name and location.

 

• This shortcut is consistent across nearly all Windows-based applications (Excel, PowerPoint, Notepad, browsers, etc.), making it one of the most universally recognised keyboard shortcuts.

 

• On Mac, the equivalent shortcut is Cmd + S.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ctrl + F opens the "Find" dialog box to search text within the document.

 

• Other common MS-Word shortcuts include Ctrl + P (Print), Ctrl + Z (Undo), and Ctrl + N (New document).

 

NOTE

 

• Alt + S (Option 1): Not the standard save shortcut in MS-Word; Alt-based shortcuts are typically used to access the Ribbon menu options.

 

• Alt + F (Option 2): Opens the File menu/Backstage view in MS-Word via the Ribbon shortcut system, not a direct save command.

 

• Ctrl + F (Option 4): Used to Find text in the document, not to save the file.

question: Which indigenous aircraft carrier was delivered to Indian Navy on July 28, 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is INS Vikrant.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• INS Vikrant, India's first indigenously designed and built aircraft carrier, was delivered to the Indian Navy by Cochin Shipyard Limited (CSL) on 28 July 2022. (आईएनएस विक्रांत — पहला स्वदेशी विमानवाहक पोत)

 

• It was formally commissioned into service on 2 September 2022 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, at Kochi, Kerala.

 

• The carrier is named after India's first aircraft carrier, the erstwhile INS Vikrant, which played a key role in the 1971 Indo-Pak War and was decommissioned in 1997.

 

• With INS Vikrant, India joined a select group of nations capable of designing and building their own aircraft carriers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• INS Vikrant is also referred to by its project name "Indigenous Aircraft Carrier-1 (IAC-1)".

 

• It can operate aircraft such as the MiG-29K fighters and various helicopters, using a STOBAR (Short Take-Off But Arrested Recovery) configuration.

 

NOTE

 

• INS Arihant (Option 1): India's first indigenously built nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarine (SSBN), not an aircraft carrier.

 

• INS Shivaji (Option 3): A shore establishment (naval training facility) in Lonavala, not an aircraft carrier.

 

• INS Vikramaditya (Option 4): India's other operational aircraft carrier, but it was originally the Russian carrier Admiral Gorshkov, refitted and commissioned into Indian Navy service in 2013 — not indigenously built.

question: Dhuska is the most popular food item of state of ______ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jharkhand.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dhuska is a popular traditional snack of Jharkhand, made from a deep-fried batter of rice and lentils (chana dal), typically served with aloo dum (spicy potato curry) or ghugni (chickpea curry). (धुस्का — झारखंड का पारंपरिक व्यंजन)

 

• It is a common street food and breakfast item across Jharkhand, especially in areas like Ranchi, and holds cultural significance in the state's tribal/local cuisine.

 

• Jharkhand's cuisine also features other well-known dishes such as Litti-Chokha, Rugra, and Pittha.

 

• Jharkhand was carved out of Bihar as a separate state on 15 November 2000.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Jharkhand is also known for its rich mineral resources and is often called the "land of forests".

 

• Similar deep-fried snacks appear in neighbouring regional cuisines, but "Dhuska" as a named dish is specifically associated with Jharkhand.

 

NOTE

 

• Punjab (Option 1): Known for dishes like Sarson da Saag and Makki di Roti, Chole Bhature, not Dhuska.

 

• Kerala (Option 3): Known for dishes like Appam, Puttu, and Sadya, not Dhuska.

 

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 4): Known for spicy dishes like Gongura Pachadi and Pesarattu, not Dhuska.
